extra.message: User input from request.POST['name'] is interpolated directly into SQL query using Python string formatting (% operator) at line 43: "VALUES ('%(name)s')" % {'name': name}. This allows SQL injection attacks. An attacker can supply a name like "'); DROP TABLE students; --" to execute arbitrary SQL commands.

Jinja2 template autoescape is disabled (autoescape=False). This disables automatic HTML escaping of template variables, making the application vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks whenever user-controlled data is rendered without explicit escaping using | e filter.

cwe: CWE-80: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page

extra.message: User-controlled data (course.title and course.description) is rendered without HTML escaping. With autoescape=False in app.py, this allows stored XSS attacks. An attacker can inject malicious JavaScript through course title/description fields which executes when users view the courses list.

User-controlled data (course.title, course.description, review.review_text, student.name) is rendered without HTML escaping on lines 14, 15, 22, and 49. With autoescape=False, this allows stored XSS. Attackers can inject malicious scripts via course/review data that execute when viewing course details.

User-controlled student name is rendered without HTML escaping ({{ name }}). With autoescape=False, this allows stored XSS if an attacker can inject malicious JavaScript in student names via the SQL injection vulnerability or direct input.

User-controlled course title and description are rendered without HTML escaping. Note: student.name is properly escaped with | e filter, but course data is not. This allows stored XSS via course data.
User-controlled student.name (line 25) and course.name (line 28) are rendered without HTML escaping. This allows stored XSS via student/course names.
User-controlled course.title is rendered without HTML escaping in the card title. Note: line 10 has proper escaping with | e, but line 32 does not. This allows stored XSS.

CSRF middleware is commented out, leaving all POST endpoints unprotected. This allows Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks. An attacker can craft a malicious page that submits forms to create students, courses, reviews, or logout users without their consent.

Session cookie is created with httponly=False, allowing JavaScript access to the session cookie. Combined with XSS vulnerabilities, this enables attackers to steal session tokens and hijack user accounts.
Debug mode is enabled (debug=True) in production application. This can expose sensitive information like stack traces, environment variables, and configuration details to attackers when errors occur.

cwe: CWE-215: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Debugging Code

extra.message: MD5 hash is used for password hashing without salt. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password storage. Passwords should be hashed using strong algorithms like bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2 with proper salting.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
